message.content:
The title of “best” movie is always a bit subjective, but if you’re looking for the film that most critics, audiences, and award bodies crowned as the standout of 2020, **“Nomadland”** is the one that comes up most often. ### Why “Nomadland”? | Category | Details | |----------|---------| | **Release** | 2020 (premiered at Sundance, released widely in 2021) | | **Director** | Chloé Zhao | | **Cast** | Frances McDormand (lead), David Strathairn, and many real-life nomads | | **Accolades** | • 2021 Academy Awards – Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress (Frances McDormand)
• 2021 Golden Globes – Best Motion Picture – Drama
• 2021 BAFTA – Best Film, Best Director | | **Critical Reception** | Rotten Tomatoes: 98% fresh; Metacritic: 88/100 (universal acclaim) | | **Cultural Impact** | Sparked conversations about the gig economy, rural America, and the definition of “home.” | ### Other strong contenders from 2020 | Film | Highlights | |------|------------| | **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | Political drama that won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay; praised for its timely themes. | | **“Soul”** | Pixar’s animated masterpiece that won Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score. | | **“Minari”** | A quiet, heartfelt story about a Korean-American family that earned a Best Supporting Actor Oscar. | | **“Promising Young Woman”** | Bold feminist thriller that won Best Original Screenplay. | ### Bottom line If you’re looking for the film that dominated the awards circuit and captured the zeitgeist of 2020, “Nomadland” is the clear frontrunner. It blends a powerful narrative with stunning visuals and earned the highest honors at the Oscars, making it the most celebrated movie of that year.
